import { formatDateTime, formatRate, formatTenure } from '../../domain/format'
import { Decimal, formatMoney } from '../../domain/money'
import type { HistoryEntry as Entry } from '../../storage/history'
import { copy } from '../copy'

interface HistoryEntryProps {
  entry: Entry
  onRestore: (entry: Entry, button: HTMLButtonElement) => void
  onDelete: (id: string) => void
}

/** One saved calculation: three lines (spec §7) and its Restore/Delete buttons (D-29 names). */
export function HistoryEntry({ entry, onRestore, onDelete }: HistoryEntryProps) {
  const { input, currency } = entry
  const line1 = copy.history.line1(
    formatMoney(new Decimal(input.amount), currency),
    formatRate(new Decimal(input.rate)),
    formatTenure(input.tenure, input.unit),
  )
  // The stored payment was checked against the recomputed one on load (§9.2), so they are equal.
  const line2 = copy.history.line2(formatMoney(new Decimal(entry.monthlyPayment), currency))
  const datetime = formatDateTime(new Date(entry.createdAt))

  return (
    <li className="history-entry" data-entry-id={entry.id}>
      <div className="entry-text">
        <p className="entry-line1">{line1}</p>
        <p>{line2}</p>
        <p className="entry-time">{copy.history.line3(datetime)}</p>
      </div>
      <div className="entry-actions">
        <button
          type="button"
          className="secondary"
          data-action="restore"
          aria-label={copy.history.restoreName(line1, datetime)}
          onClick={(event) => onRestore(entry, event.currentTarget)}
        >
          {copy.history.restore}
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          className="secondary"
          aria-label={copy.history.deleteName(line1, datetime)}
          onClick={() => onDelete(entry.id)}
        >
          {copy.history.delete}
        </button>
      </div>
    </li>
  )
}

  // closing) run first, so focus never lands behind a still-open modal.
  useEffect(() => {
    const target = pendingFocus.current
    if (!target) return
    pendingFocus.current = null
    if (target === 'heading') headingRef.current?.focus()
    else if (target === 'clearAll') clearAllRef.current?.focus()
    else {
      const selector = `[data-entry-id="${CSS.escape(target.restore)}"] [data-action="restore"]`
      listRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(selector)?.focus()

    if (!available) return

      if (focusedId && !next.some((e) => e.id === focusedId)) pendingFocus.current = 'heading'
      dispatch({ type: 'historyReloaded', entries: next })

    return () => window.removeEventListener('storage', onStorage)

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-10-18 15:09 PKT

## Mini-gate G4.5: saved calculations done

Group 5 (S-11, S-12) is built and independently reviewed, with **0 blocking findings**. The commits are `ec76864`..`2aeaa66`.

**What was built**
- **Auto-save:** each successful calculation is saved; newest first, at most 20, an exact repeat skipped, each entry showing three lines.
- **Restore:** fills the form, switches and remembers the currency, recalculates, and leaves focus on the Restore button.
- **Delete:** removes by id, with focus moving to the next entry, else the previous one, else the heading.
- **Clear all:** asks for confirmation in a native dialog, with explicit focus at every step.
- **Two-tab safety:** every save and delete re-reads storage first, and the list follows changes made in other tabs.
- **Corrupt or tampered data:** dropped silently.
- **Failures:** blocked storage shows "unavailable"; a failed delete or Clear all keeps the entries and says so.

**Evidence**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Full E2E suite (clean run, all 3 browsers) | **452 of 453**: the frozen suite plus 6 reviewer tests |
| Vitest, lint, format, typecheck | 297 of 297 tests passed; all other checks exit 0 |
| Freeze check | Only the authorised changes (D-46, D-48, D-54/55) |
| `code-reviewer` | **0 blocking.** Clean results from hostile stores (including 10,000 entries), interleaved two-tab writes, Escape pressed twice, keyboard-only deletes and a near-full storage quota. |

**Fixed after review** (D-58):
- **G45-1:** focus fell to the page body when another tab disabled Clear all mid-dialog. It now falls back to the heading.
- **G45-2:** a tampered entry could show the year "10000". The year is now checked in local time.
- **G45-3:** a tampered 10,000-entry store loaded slowly. Validation now stops after 20 valid entries.

**A slip of mine:** I ran Playwright while the reviewer was running it too, and the runs collided. The figures above are from a clean re-run, and the two runs won't overlap again.

**Your decision: the single Firefox failure (G45-4, AC-8.1)**

Both the reviewer and I proved with a page containing no app code that Playwright's Firefox **keeps focus on the last control when you Tab past it**, while Chromium and WebKit don't. The frozen test's line `expect(resetBtn).not.toBeFocused()` after that Tab is therefore testing a browser quirk. The app's tab order is correct, and the same test confirms the disabled Clear all is skipped.

```
import { Fragment } from 'react'

/**
 * Renders text with a line-break opportunity (<wbr>) after every comma, so long amounts wrap
 * between digit groups instead of mid-number (G4.3/D-54 review D54-3). <wbr> adds no text, so
 * textContent and accessible names are unchanged.
 */
export function BreakAfterCommas({ text }: { text: string }) {
  const parts = text.split(',')
  return (
    <>
      {parts.map((part, i) => (
        <Fragment key={i}>
          {part}
          {i < parts.length - 1 && (
            <>
              ,<wbr />
            </>
          )}
        </Fragment>
      ))}
    </>
  )
}
```

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-10-18 16:41 PKT

Written for: a designer or AI design tool that has never seen this project.

The brief is here: **[EMI Calculator Design Brief](https://claude.ai/artifact/4z1MDYd5rMs6mfcDZ34ntw)**. It's private: it only opens for you until you share it from the page's Share menu, or you can copy the text straight into the design tool.

It reads like a brief to a designer: it explains the product and leaves all the creative decisions to them. It contains:

- **The ask and the people:** the three users, their situations, and what the design has to do for each.
- **What exists today:** two embedded screenshots, desktop light and phone dark.
- **The screen layout,** **every state to design** (15 rows), and **content extremes** using real strings, up to `Rs 75,000,000,000,000,003.34`.
- **What's fixed, and why:** the rules the tests enforce:
  - order and the side-by-side or stacked layouts;
  - exact copy;
  - 4.5:1 and 3:1 contrast;
  - a focus outline of at least 2 px;
  - 44 px tap targets;
  - system fonts only;
  - plain CSS;
  - the colour token names.
- **Where they have freedom,** and **what to deliver.** Ideally the deliverable is one plain-CSS stylesheet written against the existing class names.
- **Reference material:** the markup skeleton with classes, the current tokens, and every word on the screen.

Two things to know when you use it:

- **The new design must fit the existing constraints, or it comes back as proposals.** The brief tells the designer to list any text, markup or rule changes separately, so you can approve or decline each one, as we've done for everything else.
- **This is planning only.** When a design comes back, I'll implement it as its own change cycle: CSS against the frozen tests, a full `verify`, an independent review and a mini-gate.

The group 6 review is still running in the background. I'll report it when it finishes.

```bash
cd "C:/Users/arslan.NINEALPHA/muhammad-arslan-calculator" && python -I - <<'EOF'
src = open('design/emi-pastel-redesign/styles/app.css', encoding='utf-8').read()
start_base = src.index('/* ---------- 2. Base')
tokens, rest = src[:start_base], src[start_base:]

def rep(text, old, new, label):
    assert text.count(old) == 1, f"{label}: expected exactly one match"
    return text.replace(old, new)

header = ("/* Design tokens: the \"Soft ledger\" pastel redesign (D-62), copied from\n"
          "   design/emi-pastel-redesign/styles/app.css section 1. Tested token names are unchanged. */\n\n")
tokens = header + tokens[tokens.index('/* ---------- 1. Tokens'):]

# 1. No overflow masking: the layout must genuinely not overflow (AC-5.1/5.6 stay honest).
rest = rep(rest, "  overflow-x: hidden; /* safety net; layout itself never overflows */\n", "", "overflow-x")
# 2. Field-error elements are aria-live regions that must stay in the accessibility tree when
#    empty, so new errors are announced (spec §8.3). Hide only the icon.
rest = rep(rest, ".field-error:empty { display: none; }\n",
           ".field-error:empty::before { content: none; } /* keep the live region; hide only the icon (D-64) */\n",
           "field-error empty")
# 3. Fatal-error screen (handoff step 5; not in the bundle's CSS).
rest += """
/* ---------- 13. Fatal error (handoff step 5) ----------------------------- */

.fatal {
  max-width: 280px;
  margin: 20vh auto 0;
  padding: var(--space-4);
  text-align: center;
  color: var(--text);
  background: var(--bg);
  font-size: 18px;
  font-weight: 650;
}
"""
rest = ("/* Layout and components: the \"Soft ledger\" pastel redesign (D-62), adapted from\n"
        "   design/emi-pastel-redesign/styles/app.css with the deviations recorded in D-64. */\n\n") + rest
open('src/ui/theme.css', 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n').write(tokens)
open('src/ui/app.css', 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n').write(rest)
print("theme.css", tokens.count('\n'), "lines | app.css", rest.count('\n'), "lines")
EOF

const pw = require('@playwright/test');
(async () => {
  for (const name of ['chromium', 'firefox', 'webkit']) {
    for (const width of [1280, 360]) {
      const b = await pw[name].launch(); const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width, height: 900 } });
      await p.goto(process.argv[2]);
      const times = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        await p.getByRole('button', { name: 'Reset' }).click();
        await p.getByLabel(/^Loan amount/).fill('1000000000000000'); await p.getByLabel('Annual interest rate (%)').fill('75');
        await p.getByLabel('Loan tenure', { exact: true }).fill('100');
        const ms = await p.evaluate(() => new Promise((resolve) => {
          const start = performance.now();
          const obs = new MutationObserver(() => {
            if (document.querySelectorAll('table tr').length >= 1201) { obs.disconnect(); requestAnimationFrame(() => resolve(performance.now() - start)); }
          });
          obs.observe(document.body, { childList: true, subtree: true });
          document.querySelector('button.primary').click();
        }));
        times.push(Math.round(ms));
      }
      console.log(name.padEnd(9), String(width).padStart(4) + 'px', 'L-MAX click -> 1,200 rows + next frame (ms):', times.join(', '));
      await b.close();
    }
  }
})();

  'as designed': '',
  'no card shadow': '.card{box-shadow:none!important}',
  'border-collapse: collapse': '.schedule table{border-collapse:collapse!important}',
  'no zebra / year-end / paid-off': '.schedule tbody tr td{background:transparent!important;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border)!important;font-weight:inherit!important}',
  'th not sticky': '.schedule th{position:static!important}',
  'no tabular-nums': '.schedule table,input,select,.figure dd,.entry-text p{font-variant-numeric:normal!important}',
};
(async () => {
  const b = await pw.webkit.launch();
  for (const [label, css] of Object.entries(variants)) {
    const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1280, height: 900 } });

      await p.getByLabel('Loan tenure', { exact: true }).fill('100');
      times.push(Math.round(await p.evaluate(() => new Promise((resolve) => {
        const start = performance.now();
        const obs = new MutationObserver(() => { if (document.querySelectorAll('table tr').length >= 1201) { obs.disconnect(); requestAnimationFrame(() => resolve(performance.now() - start)); } });
        obs.observe(document.body, { childList: true, subtree: true }); document.querySelector('button.primary').click();
      }))));
    }
    times.sort((a, b) => a - b);
    console.log(label.padEnd(32), 'median', String((times[1] + times[2]) / 2).padStart(5), 'ms  (all:', times.join(', ') + ')');
    await p.close();
  }
  await b.close();
})();
EOF

})();

> **Which visuals should the app show? Pick any. Each would sit in the results card, below the figures, with a short text summary so screen-reader users get the same information.**

  - **Balance over time**: An area chart of the remaining balance falling from the loan amount to zero, month by month (1 to 1,200 points). Serves 'what do I still owe?' (R-3).
  - **Payment make-up over time**: A stacked chart of each payment split into interest and principal over the loan. It shows interest shrinking as principal grows, which is the key insight for advisors explaining a quote (R-2) and for borrowers weighing early repayment (R-3).
  - **Yearly summary chart**: Bars per year of interest vs principal paid. This is backlog story S-19 brought into v1, so it's the largest change: new story scope plus its table equivalent.

from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP
src = open("bounds_v2.py", encoding="utf-8").read(); ns = {}; exec(src.split("# 1. Smallest safe amount")[0], ns)
r2, emi = ns["r2"], ns["emi"]
def sched(P, rate, n):
    P, rate = D(P), D(rate); r = rate / 1200; bal = P; rows = []
    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        it = r2(bal * rate / 1200)
        if k < n: pay = r2(emi(bal, r, n - k + 1)); pr = pay - it
        else: pr = bal; pay = pr + it
        bal -= pr; rows.append((k, pay, it, pr, bal))
    return rows
pct = lambda a, b: (D(100) * a / b).quantize(D("0.1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
fmt = lambda x: f"{int(x):,}" + "." + f"{x:.2f}".split(".")[1]
for name, P, rate, n in [("L-A", "1000000", "12", 12), ("L-B", "2500000", "18", 60), ("L-C", "120000", "0", 12), ("L-D", "100000", "10", 1), ("L-Z3", "1000", "0", 3)]:
    rows = sched(P, rate, n); ti = sum(x[2] for x in rows); tp = sum(x[1] for x in rows)
    ip = pct(ti, tp); lp = D(100) - ip
    first, last = rows[0], rows[-1]
    print(f"{name}: interest {ip}% / loan {lp}% of total | first payment interest share {pct(first[2], first[1])}% | last payment interest share {pct(last[2], last[1])}%")
    years = [rows[i:i + 12] for i in range(0, n, 12)]
    for y, chunk in enumerate(years, 1):
        print(f"     year {y} ({len(chunk)} months): interest {fmt(sum(c[2] for c in chunk))} principal {fmt(sum(c[3] for c in chunk))} balance at end {fmt(chunk[-1][4])}")
# a non-multiple-of-12 case
rows = sched("100000", "10", 18)
print("18-month 100000 @10%:", [(len(rows[i:i+12]), fmt(sum(c[2] for c in rows[i:i+12])), fmt(sum(c[3] for c in rows[i:i+12]))) for i in range(0, 18, 12)])
EOF

# Proposal: visuals in the results (charts)

**Status:** Proposed by Claude Code, 2026-10-18, for owner approval. Nothing here is built or added to the ACs yet.
**Requested by:** the owner ("add a few visuals, like charts"). The owner chose all four visuals.

## Summary

Four visuals, all inside the results card, all built from the schedule the app already computes:

| # | Visual | Story | Role / job | What it answers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cost split bar | **S-20** (new) | R-1 / J-2 | "How much of what I repay is interest?" |
| 2 | Balance over time | **S-21** (new) | R-3 / J-8 | "What will I still owe, and when?" |
| 3 | Payment make-up over time | **S-22** (new) | R-2 / J-5 | "Why does the interest part shrink?" |
| 4 | Yearly summary (chart + table) | **S-19** (Backlog → v1) | R-3 / J-9 | "How much interest did each year cost?" |

**Order in the results card:**
1. the three figures and the rounding note (unchanged);
2. Cost breakdown;
3. Balance over time;
4. Interest and principal in each payment;
5. Yearly summary;
6. the Repayment schedule (unchanged, still last).

## Rules every visual follows

- **No new dependencies.** Each chart is hand-built inline SVG, drawn in React from the existing `CalculatedLoan`. There's no charting library and no network.
- **Never colour alone.** Each chart sits in a `<figure>` whose `<figcaption>` holds a one-sentence text summary (exact wording below). The data is also always available as a table: the existing schedule, plus a new yearly table. The SVG itself is `aria-hidden="true"`, because the figcaption and the tables carry the information for assistive technology.
- **Legends:** charts with two series (principal and interest) show an HTML legend, plus direct labels where they fit. One-series charts have no legend; the title names the series.
- **Colour:** two categorical series in a fixed order, Principal first and Interest second, the same in every chart. The pairs are checked with the data-visualisation validator script against the light and dark surfaces, not by eye. The marks may need deeper shades than the pastel fills to reach 3:1 against the surface (WCAG 1.4.11). Text uses text tokens only.
- **One axis per chart,** no dual axes. Axes and grid are kept quiet.
- **Hover:** a tooltip on the balance, payment and yearly charts (crosshair or per-bar) showing the exact values. Keyboard and screen-reader users get the same values from the tables.
- **Performance:** each series is a single SVG `<path>`, never 1,200 elements, so L-MAX (1,200 months) keeps AC-10.8's 1-second budget.
- **Layout:** fluid width with no fixed pixel sizes, so there's no horizontal page scroll from 180 px up; works in both themes.

## New domain functions (pure, unit-tested)

- `costSplit(loan): { interestPercent: Decimal, loanPercent: Decimal }`
  - `interestPercent = round1(100 × totalInterest / totalPayable)`, where `round1` rounds half-up to 1 dp;
  - `loanPercent = 100 − interestPercent`, so the two always sum to ex

"""Record G3b approval (D-66, D-67) and the three copy answers in the spec. Each replacement must match once."""
import sys

root = sys.argv[1]


def edit(rel, pairs):
    path = f"{root}/{rel}"
    s = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    for old, new in pairs:
        assert s.count(old) == 1, f"{rel}: expected exactly one match for: {old[:80]!r}"
        s = s.replace(old, new)
    open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n").write(s)

/** Integer cents -> "1,234.56" (independent of the app's formatter). */
export function fmtCents(c: bigint): string {
  const whole = (c / 100n).toString().replace(/\B(?=(\d{3})+(?!\d))/g, ',')
  return `${whole}.${String(c % 100n).padStart(2, '0')}`
}
/** Moves the pointer over item k of n inside the figure's [data-hit-area] (D-66). */
export async function hoverItem(figure: Locator, k: number, n: number): Promise<void> {
  const area = figure.locator('[data-hit-area]')
  await expect(area, 'the figure has exactly one [data-hit-area]').toHaveCount(1)
  const b = await box(area)
  await area.hover({ position: { x: ((k - 0.5) / n) * b.width, y: b.height / 2 } })
}
/** Hover item k of n and expect the single tooltip to read exactly `text`. */

/**
 * Validate a categorical chart palette against the computable data-viz checks.
 *
 * Design-system-agnostic: feed it ANY palette's hex values plus the mode and
 * surface, and it computes - never eyeballs - the five checks that can be
 * measured from color alone:
 *
 *   2. Lightness band   - OKLCH L within the mode's band
 *   3. Chroma floor     - OKLCH C >= floor (below it a hue reads as gray)
 *   4. CVD separation   - OKLab Delta E (×100) between slots under simulated protan/deutan
 *                         (tritan reported); adjacent pairs by default, pairs:"all"
 *                         for scatter/bubble/maps
 *   4b. Normal-vision floor - worst OKLab Delta E (×100) on the active pairlist
 *       (adjacent by default; all pairs with --pairs all) under unsimulated vision;
 *                         full-color readers must be able to tell neighbors apart too
 *   5. Contrast vs surface - WCAG ratio of each mark against the chart surface
 *
 * Checks 1 (fixed hue order) and 6 (values are from the documented palette) are
 * structural rules the skill enforces, not measurable from hexes alone.
 *
 * Usage (node):
 *   node validate_palette.js "#2a78d6,#eb6834,#1baf7a,#eda100,#e87ba4,#008300,#6250d6,#e34948" --mode light
 *   node validate_palette.js "#256abf,#199e70,..." --mode dark --surface "#1a1a19"
 *   node validate_palette.js "#86b6ef,#5598e7,#256abf,#104281" --ordinal
 *
 * Usage (browser - as a module script):
 *   <body data-palette="#2a78d6,#eb6834,..." data-mode="light">
 *   <script type="module" src="validate_palette.js"></script>
 *   -> logs a console.table of the report and console.warn on any FAIL.
 *
 * Exit code 0 unless a check hard-FAILs; 1 on any FAIL. WARN bands do not fail:
 * adjacent CVD in the 6-8 floor band, and contrast in the sub-3:1 relief band,
 * are reported as WARNs and still exit 0 (each is legal only with mandatory
 * secondary encoding: direct labels, gaps, or texture). The normal-vision floor
 * is a hard gate: a worst unsimulated pair below 15 FAILs the run.
 */
// -- thresholds ----------------------------------------------------------------
// Delta E is Euclidean distance in OKLab ×100. The CVD thresholds are calibrated to
// the Machado-Oliveira-Fernandes (2009) severity-1.0 simulation below - the sim
// model is part of the standard, not an implementation detail (swapping in e.g.

// Loan summaries for the visuals (spec §3.1.1, D-65). Pure, exact Decimal arithmetic.
import { Decimal } from './money'
import type { CalculatedLoan } from './types'

/** One calendar-free "year" of the schedule: 12 months, or fewer for the final group. */
export interface YearRow {
  year: number
  months: number
  interest: Decimal
  principal: Decimal
  /** Balance after the group's last month. */
  balance: Decimal
}

const HUNDRED = new Decimal(100)
const round1 = (x: Decimal) => x.toDecimalPlaces(1, Decimal.ROUND_HALF_UP)

/** interestPercent = 100 × totalInterest / totalPayable, half-up to 1 dp; loanPercent = 100 − it. */
export function costSplit(loan: CalculatedLoan): {
  interestPercent: Decimal
  loanPercent: Decimal
} {
  const interestPercent = round1(loan.totalInterest.times(HUNDRED).div(loan.totalPayable))
  // Derived by subtraction so the two parts always sum to exactly 100.0.
  return { interestPercent, loanPercent: HUNDRED.minus(interestPercent) }
}

/** 100 × interest / payment, half-up to 1 dp. */
export function interestShare(payment: Decimal, interest: Decimal): Decimal {
  if (payment.isZero()) return new Decimal(0) // unreachable for validated loans; never divide by 0
  return round1(interest.times(HUNDRED).div(payment))
}

/** Groups of 12 schedule rows (the last shorter if needed), with exact sums. */
export function yearlySummary(loan: CalculatedLoan): YearRow[] {
  const years: YearRow[] = []
  const zero = new Decimal(0)
  for (let start = 0; start < loan.rows.length; start += 12) {
    const group = loan.rows.slice(start, start + 12)
    const last = group[group.length - 1]
    if (!last) break
    years.push({
      year: years.length + 1,
      months: group.length,
      interest: group.reduce((sum, row) => sum.plus(row.interest), zero),
      principal: group.reduce((sum, row) => sum.plus(row.principal), zero),
      balance: last.balance,
    })
  }
  return years
}
```

// Shared chart geometry (spec §8.3.2, D-66, D-68). Every chart uses the same band layout:
// item k (0-based) of n occupies [k/n, (k+1)/n] of the plot width, so its centre is at
// (k + 0.5) / n, which is where the hover hook in the DOM contract expects it.
import { useState, type PointerEvent } from 'react'
import { Decimal } from '../../../domain/money'

/** The SVG plot is drawn in this viewBox and stretched to the card (preserveAspectRatio="none"). */
export const VIEW_W = 1000
export const VIEW_H = 100

/**
 * A dimensionless 0..1 ratio for drawing. Computed in Decimal; only the ratio (never a money
 * value) becomes a JS number, and only for pixel geometry (D-68).
 */
export function ratio(value: Decimal, max: Decimal): number {
  if (max.isZero()) return 0
  return value.div(max).toDecimalPlaces(6).toNumber()
}

/** y coordinate (0 = top) for a ratio of the plot height. */
const y = (r: number) => VIEW_H - r * VIEW_H

/**
 * One closed path: a stepped band between `bottom` and `top` ratios for every item.
 * Drawing all items as one path keeps 1,200 months to a single SVG element.
 */
export function stepBandPath(top: number[], bottom?: number[]): string {
  const n = top.length
  if (n === 0) return ''
  const w = VIEW_W / n
  const upper: string[] = []
  const lower: string[] = []
  for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
    const x0 = (k * w).toFixed(3)
    const x1 = ((k + 1) * w).toFixed(3)
    const t = y(top[k] ?? 0).toFixed(3)
    const b = y(bottom?.[k] ?? 0).toFixed(3)
    upper.push(`L${x0},${t}L${x1},${t}`)
    lower.unshift(`L${x1},${b}L${x0},${b}`)
  }
  const start = y(bottom?.[0] ?? 0).toFixed(3)
  return `M0,${start}${upper.join('')}${lower.join('')}Z`
}

/** One path of separate bars (one per item) between `bottom` and `top` ratios. */
export function barsPath(top: number[], bottom: number[], fill = 0.64): string {
  const n = top.length
  const band = VIEW_W / n
  const width = band * fill
  return top
    .map((t, k) => {
      const x = k * band + (band - width) / 2
      const yTop = y(t)
      const yBottom = y(bottom[k] ?? 0)
      const h = yBottom - yTop
      if (h <= 0) return ''
      return `M${x.toFixed(3)},${yTop.toFixed(3)}h${width.toFixed(3)}v${h.toFixed(3)}h${(-width).toFixed(3)}Z`
    })
    .join('')
}

/** The x position, as a percentage of the plot width, of the centre of item k of n. */
export const centrePercent = (k: number, n: number) => ((k + 0.5) / n) * 100

/** Pointer hover over the plot: which item (0-based) is under the pointer, or null. */
export function useBandHover(count: number) {
  const [index, setIndex] = useState<number | null>(null)
  const onPointerMove = (event: PointerEvent<Element>) => {
    const rect = event.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect()
    if (rect.width <= 0) return
    const f = (event.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width
    setIndex(Math.min(count - 1, Math.max(0, Math.floor(f * count))))
  }
  const onPointerLeave = () => setIndex(null)

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { copy } from '../../copy'
import { centrePercent } from './chartGeometry'

/** HTML legend (spec §8.3.2): Principal first, Interest second, in every chart. */
export function Legend({ first = copy.chart.series.principal }: { first?: string }) {
  return (
    <ul className="chart-legend">
      <li>
        <span className="swatch swatch-principal" aria-hidden="true" />
        {first}
      </li>
      <li>
        <span className="swatch swatch-interest" aria-hidden="true" />
        {copy.chart.series.interest}
      </li>
    </ul>
  )
}

/** First and last item numbers under the plot (numbers only; no new words, D-68). */
export function AxisEnds({ count }: { count: number }) {
  return (
    <div className="chart-axis">
      <span>1</span>
      {count > 1 && <span>{count}</span>}
    </div>
  )
}

/** The pointer tooltip, kept inside the plot's width at both ends. */
export function Tooltip({ index, count, children }: { index: number | null; count: number; children: ReactNode }) {
  if (index === null) return null
  const left = centrePercent(index, count)
  return (
    <div role="tooltip" className="chart-tooltip" style={{ left: `${left}%`, transform: `translateX(-${left}%)` }}>
      {children}
    </div>
  )
}

/** A faint highlight of the hovered band (decorative; not a data mark). */
export function HoverBand({ index, count }: { index: number | null; count: number }) {
  if (index === null) return null
  const width = 1000 / count
  return <rect className="chart-hover-band" x={index * width} y={0} width={width} height={100} />
}

import { formatMoney } from '../../../domain/money'
import { Decimal } from '../../../domain/money'
import type { CalculatedLoan, Currency } from '../../../domain/types'
import { copy } from '../../copy'
import { AxisEnds, HoverBand, Tooltip } from './ChartParts'
import { VIEW_H, VIEW_W, groupCount, ratio, stepBandPath, useBandHover } from './chartGeometry'

/** S-21: the balance after each month, as one stepped area falling to zero. */
export function BalanceChart({ loan, currency }: { loan: CalculatedLoan; currency: Currency }) {
  const { rows, input } = loan
  const n = rows.length
  const { index, handlers } = useBandHover(n)
  const tops = rows.map((row) => ratio(row.balance, input.amount))
  const summary = copy.chart.balance.summary(
    formatMoney(input.amount, currency),
    formatMoney(new Decimal(0), currency),
    groupCount(n),
    n,
  )
  const hovered = index === null ? undefined : rows[index]
  return (
    <div className="chart-block">

            <path className="mark-principal" data-series="balance" d={stepBandPath(tops)} />

        <figcaption>{summary}</figcaption>

```
import { formatPercent } from '../../../domain/format'
import { formatMoney } from '../../../domain/money'
import { interestShare } from '../../../domain/summary'
import type { CalculatedLoan, Currency } from '../../../domain/types'
import { copy } from '../../copy'
import { AxisEnds, HoverBand, Legend, Tooltip } from './ChartParts'
import { VIEW_H, VIEW_W, ratio, stepBandPath, useBandHover } from './chartGeometry'

/** S-22: each payment stacked as principal (bottom) and interest (top). */
export function PaymentMakeupChart({ loan, currency }: { loan: CalculatedLoan; currency: Currency }) {
  const { rows } = loan
  const n = rows.length
  const { index, handlers } = useBandHover(n)
  const max = rows.reduce((m, row) => (row.payment.gt(m) ? row.payment : m), rows[0]!.payment)
  const principalTops = rows.map((row) => ratio(row.principal, max))
  const paymentTops = rows.map((row) => ratio(row.payment, max))
  const first = rows[0]!
  const last = rows[n - 1]!
  const summary = copy.chart.makeup.summary(
    formatPercent(interestShare(first.payment, first.interest)),
    formatPercent(interestShare(last.payment, last.interest)),
  )
  const hovered = index === null ? undefined : rows[index]
  return (
    <div className="chart-block">
      <h3 className="chart-title">{copy.chart.makeup.title}</h3>
      <figure className="chart">
        <div className="chart-plot-wrap">
          <svg
            className="chart-plot"
            viewBox={`0 0 ${VIEW_W} ${VIEW_H}`}
            preserveAspectRatio="none"
            aria-hidden="true"
            data-hit-area=""
            {...handlers}
          >
            <HoverBand index={index} count={n} />
            <path className="mark-principal" data-series="principal" d={stepBandPath(principalTops)} />
            <path
              className="mark-interest"
              data-series="interest"
              d={stepBandPath(paymentTops, principalTops)}
            />
          </svg>
          <Tooltip index={index} count={n}>
            {hovered &&
              copy.chart.makeup.tooltip(
                hovered.month,
                formatMoney(hovered.principal, currency),
                formatMoney(hovered.interest, currency),
              )}
          </Tooltip>
        </div>
        <AxisEnds count={n} />
        <Legend />
        <figcaption>{summary}</figcaption>
      </figure>
    </div>
  )
}
```

```
import { formatAmount, formatMoney } from '../../../domain/money'
import { yearlySummary } from '../../../domain/summary'
import type { CalculatedLoan, Currency } from '../../../domain/types'
import { copy } from '../../copy'
import { AxisEnds, HoverBand, Legend, Tooltip } from './ChartParts'
import { VIEW_H, VIEW_W, barsPath, ratio, useBandHover } from './chartGeometry'

/** S-19: interest vs principal per year, as stacked bars plus the same figures in a table. */
export function YearlySummary({ loan, currency }: { loan: CalculatedLoan; currency: Currency }) {
  const years = yearlySummary(loan)
  const n = years.length
  const { index, handlers } = useBandHover(n)
  const totals = years.map((y) => y.principal.plus(y.interest))
  const max = totals.reduce((m, t) => (t.gt(m) ? t : m), totals[0]!)
  const principalTops = years.map((y) => ratio(y.principal, max))
  const totalTops = totals.map((t) => ratio(t, max))
  const hovered = index === null ? undefined : years[index]
  return (
    <div className="chart-block yearly">
      <h3 id="yearly-title" className="chart-title">
        {copy.yearly.title}
      </h3>
      <figure className="chart">
        <div className="chart-plot-wrap">
          <svg
            className="chart-plot"
            viewBox={`0 0 ${VIEW_W} ${VIEW_H}`}
            preserveAspectRatio="none"
            aria-hidden="true"
            data-hit-area=""
            {...handlers}
          >
            <HoverBand index={index} count={n} />
            <path
              className="mark-principal"
              data-series="principal"
              d={barsPath(principalTops, new Array<number>(n).fill(0))}
            />
            <path className="mark-interest" data-series="interest" d={barsPath(totalTops, principalTops)} />
          </svg>
          <Tooltip index={index} count={n}>
            {hovered &&
              copy.yearly.tooltip(
                hovered.year,
                formatMoney(hovered.principal, currency),
                formatMoney(hovered.interest, currency),
              )}
          </Tooltip>
        </div>
        <AxisEnds count={n} />
        <Legend />
        <figcaption>{copy.yearly.chartCaption}</figcaption>
      </figure>
      <table className="yearly-table" aria-labelledby="yearly-title">
        <thead>
          <tr>
            {copy.yearly.cols(currency).map((col) => (
              <th key={col} scope="col">
                {col}
              </th>
            ))}
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {years.map((y) => (
            <tr key={y.year}>
              <td>{y.year}</td>
              <td>{formatAmount(y.interest)}</td>
              <td>{formatAmount(y.principal)}</td>
              <td>{formatAmount(y.balance)}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  )
}

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-10-18 19:16 PKT

You mean the **loan form** (the left card): keep it in view while you scroll through the results, instead of leaving that empty space. That's a CSS-only change and a good fit. My plan:
- **Desktop only (769 px and wider):** the form card becomes `position: sticky` and follows you down while the results scroll. Phones are unaffected, because there everything is one column.
- **Only when the window is tall enough to show the whole form.** Otherwise the bottom of the form, including Calculate, could end up out of reach on short laptop screens.
- **It stops at the end of the results,** so it never covers Saved calculations below.
- No markup, order or tab-order change, so the tests that depend on those aren't affected.

One thing to wait for first. My second `verify` run is still running in the background, checking whether that WebKit failure is a one-off. Changing the CSS mid-run would muddy that evidence, and so would running other browsers alongside it.      export interface YearRow { year: number; months: number; interest: Decimal; principal: Decimal; balance: Decimal }
     const HUNDRED = new Decimal(100)
     const round1 = (x: Decimal) => x.toDecimalPlaces(1, Decimal.ROUND_HALF_UP)
     export function costSplit(loan: CalculatedLoan) { const interestPercent = round1(loan.totalInterest.times(HUNDRED).div(loan.totalPayable)); return { interestPercent, loanPercent: HUNDRED.minus(interestPercent) } }
     export function interestShare(payment: Decimal, interest: Decimal): Decimal { if (payment.isZero()) return new Decimal(0); return round1(interest.times(HUNDRED).div(payment)) }
     export function yearlySummary(loan): YearRow[]  // groups of 12 rows; exact sums; balance = group's last balance
     ```

     import { Decimal } from './money'

### 8.3.2 Charts (D-65)

- **Order inside the results card:**
  1. the three figures and the rounding note;
  2. **Cost breakdown** (S-20);
  3. **Balance over time** (S-21);
  4. **Interest and principal in each payment** (S-22);
  5. **Yearly summary**, a chart and table (S-19);
  6. the **Repayment schedule**, still last.
- **Hand-built inline SVG,** drawn from `CalculatedLoan`. No chart library (§2) and no network.
- **Each series is one `<path>`,** never one element per month, so 1,200 months stay within AC-10.8.
- **Never colour alone:**
  - every chart has a visible text summary (its `<figcaption>`);
  - two-series charts have an HTML legend, with Principal first and Interest second in every chart;
  - the data is also in a table (the schedule, the yearly table).
- **Colour:** two categorical series in a fixed order, validated with the dataviz validator against the light and dark card surfaces. Marks reach at least 3:1 against `--surface`, and chart text uses the text tokens (AC-20.5).
- **One y-axis per chart.** Axes and grid are quiet.
- **Hover:** a pointer tooltip (`role="tooltip"`) on the balance, payment and yearly charts, with the exact values. Keyboard and screen-reader users get the same values from the tables.
- **Layout:** fluid width with no fixed pixel widths, and no horizontal page scroll (AC-20.6).

### 8.4 Theme

Resolved theme = the user's choice, or `prefers-color-scheme` when set to `system`. Apply it as `data-theme="light|dark"` on `<html>`. A tiny inline script in `index.html` applies the saved theme before first paint (wrapped in try/catch) so there is no flash of the wrong theme. Listen for `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')` changes while `system` is selected.

Starting tokens. Tests must prove ≥ 4.5:1 for these text pairs in both themes: text/bg, text/surface, text-muted/bg, text-muted/surface, error/bg, error/surface, on-primary/primary. """/**
 * True while the element's content is wider than the element. Then (and only then) the yearly
 * table's wrapper becomes a named, focusable scroll region, so keyboard users can scroll it at
 * very narrow widths without adding a tab stop at normal widths (AC-8.1, F-1, D-70).
 */
function useOverflows<T extends HTMLElement>() {
  const ref = useRef<T>(null)
  const [overflows, setOverflows] = useState(false)
  useEffect(() => {
    const el = ref.current
    if (!el || typeof ResizeObserver === 'undefined') return
    const check = () => setOverflows(el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth)
    const observer = new ResizeObserver(check)
    observer.observe(el)
    if (el.firstElementChild) observer.observe(el.firstElementChild)
    check()
    return () => observer.disconnect()
  }, [])
  return { ref, overflows }
}

> what are the gates?

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-10-18 21:56 PKT

A **gate** is a stop point at the end of each phase. I stop, show you the evidence, and wait for your "approved" or your corrections before going on. That keeps you deciding, while I build and the subagents test and review.

## The six gates

| Gate | Ends phase | What you approve | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **G1** | 1. Spec challenge | The requirements, after the spec critic attacked them | ✅ Approved |
| **G2** | 2. Scaffold | The empty project, tooling, CI files and traceability script | ✅ Approved |
| **G3** | 3. Tests first | The tests, written before the code; they are then frozen | ✅ Approved (G3b for the chart tests) |
| **G4.1–G4.6** | 4. Build | One mini-gate per story group (domain, core UI, schedule, settings, history, layout) | ✅ All approved |
| **G5** | 5. Independent review | Whole-app review until 0 blocking findings, **plus your hand check** on desktop and phone; you decide each story's Status | ⏳ Next |
| **G6** | 6. Release | README, push to GitHub, live site, smoke tests | ⏳ Later |

Your later requests (the redesign and the charts) each ended in an extra **mini-gate** of the same kind.

## What's waiting on you now: the visuals mini-gate
1. **D-68**: approve how the four charts were built?
2. **D-69**: approve the sticky form?
3. **D-70**: approve the review fixes, including the extra high-contrast borders on the headline tile and rounding note (RD-3)? Or should I drop those borders?
4. **D-64**: approve the redesign's three deviations from the design bundle? This one has been waiting since the redesign gate.
5. Add one line to the spec saying chart geometry may use plain JS numbers for ratios, while money never does?

A reply like "approve all" works, or answer them one by one. After that comes **Phase 5**: the whole-app review, then your hand check.

One thing to plan for: you'll need to create the public GitHub repo before Phase 6. CI and the live site depend on it.

**What was wrong:** my rule only turned sticky on when the browser window was at least 820 px tall. The form itself is only 544 px. Most laptop windows are 650 to 800 px tall, so for you it never stuck. My own check had used a tall window, so I missed it. That was my mistake.

**The fix:** whenever form and results sit side by side, the form sticks. If a window is too short to show the whole form, the form card scrolls on its own, so Calculate stays reachable.

**Checked in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit:**
- **1280 × 800 and 1366 × 650:** the form stays 24 px from the top while you scroll, and stops just above Saved calculations.
- **1280 × 480:** the form card scrolls on its own and stays pinned.
- **768 px and narrower:** stacked as before, not sticky.

**Recorded** (not yet committed):
- your approvals of D-64, D-68 and D-70 (including the RD-3 borders);
- the new spec line on chart drawing numbers, as D-71 in spec §8.3.2;
- under D-69, that it failed your check, why, and the fix.

The dev server at http://localhost:5173/ already has the fix. Reload the page and scroll the results.

# One-time manual step: Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions.
name: Deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

  deploy:
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    outputs:
      page_url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5

          cache: npm

        env:

      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

        with:

          done

      - run: npx playwright test

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-10-18 22:12 PKT

Not pushed yet: the last full `verify` failed, and I found the cause. A re-run with the fix is in progress, about 9 minutes.

**What failed:** 547 tests passed and 2 failed, both in WebKit.
- **[AC-1.10]:** a click timed out under load, the same intermittent failure we've seen before.
- **[AC-10.8]:** this one was real. Drawing all 1,200 rows of the largest loan took **1,133 ms against the 1-second limit**.

**The cause was my D-70 fix, not the sticky form.** The new yearly-table check forced the browser to lay out the whole page right after Calculate, inside the measured time. In WebKit alone, 8 runs each:

| Variant | Median |
|---|---|
| Current code | 223 ms |
| Sticky change removed | 274 ms (sticky isn't the cause) |
| **Forced check removed** | **114 ms** |

Under the full test suite's load, that doubled cost went over 1 second. I removed the forced check; the browser's own resize notification does the same job after layout. The yearly table still scrolls at 180 px and isn't a tab stop at normal widths, checked in all 3 browsers.

The earlier "549 of 549" green run had hidden this cost, so from now on timing-sensitive changes get a measured comparison. It's recorded as **D-72**, and deploying before Phase 5 as **D-73**.

**If this verify passes**, I'll commit, push `v1` with the tags, then merge into `main` and push. That push runs verify again on GitHub's Linux machines, then the deploy, then the smoke tests on the live site. If it fails, I'll report that rather than push.

    const counts = await Promise.all(pages.map(async (p) => { await p.goto('http://localhost:5173/'); return p.evaluate(() => new Promise((r) => { let n = 0; const t = performance.now(); const f = () => { n++; performance.now() - t < 1000 ? requestAnimationFrame(f) : r(n) }; requestAnimationFrame(f) })) }))
    console.log(bt.name(), 'rAF frames per second in 4 parallel pages:', counts.join(' '))
    await b.close()
  }
})()
EOF
NODE_PATH="$PWD/node_modules" node "$S/probe_raf.cjs"

"""Build readable transcripts and filtered raw logs from Claude Code session logs.

Usage: python -I make_transcripts.py <logs-dir> <session-id> <out-dir>
"""
import datetime as dt
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys

LOGS, SID, OUT = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
PKT = dt.timezone(dt.timedelta(hours=5))

SECRET_PATTERNS = [
    r'gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}', r'github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{40,}', r'sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}',
    r'sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{40,}', r'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}', r'[Bb]earer\s+[A-Za-z0-9\-_\.=]{30,}',
    r'-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----',
]
REMINDER = re.compile(r'', re.S)
IDE_TAGS = re.compile(r'<ide_(opened_file|selection)>.*?</ide_\1>', re.S)
KEEP_RAW_TYPES = {'user', 'assistant', 'system'}


def redact(s):
    for p in SECRET_PATTERNS:
        s = re.sub(p, '[REDACTED]', s)
    return s


def clean(s):
    return redact(REMINDER.sub('', s)).strip()


def when(ts):
    if not ts:
        return ''
    t = dt.datetime.fromisoformat(ts.replace('Z', '+00:00')).astimezone(PKT)
    return t.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M PKT')


def cut(s, n):
    s = s if isinstance(s, str) else json.dumps(s, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
    s = clean(s)
    return s if len(s) <= n else s[:n] + f'\n… [{len(s) - n:,} more characters not shown; see raw/]'


def fence(s, lang=''):
    ticks = '````' if '```' in s else '```'
    return f'{ticks}{lang}\n{s}\n{ticks}'


def load(path):
    with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        return [json.loads(line) for line in f if line.strip()]


def text_of(content):
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    out = []
    for b in content or []:
        if b.get('type') == 'text':
            out.append(b['text'])
        elif b.get('type') == 'image':
            out.append('[screenshot attached]')
    return '\n'.join(out)


def result_text(block):
    c = block.get('content')
    if isinstance(c, list):
        return '\n'.join(x.get('text', '[image]') if x.get('type') != 'image' else '[image]' for x in c)
    return c or ''

        body.append(fence(cut(inp.get('content', ''), 3000)))
    elif name == 'Agent':
        link = agent_links.get(inp.get('_id'))
        head = f"**Subagent `{inp.get('subagent_type', 'general')}`** · {inp.get('description', '')}"
        if link:
